name: Poly Styrene
who_line: Day-glo plastic against consumerism: proof you could be stylish without money.
who: Poly Styrene fronted X-Ray Spex. Before the band she ran a stall in Beaufort Market off the King’s Road, near SEX, “selling plastic trash, mainly kitsch jewellery and bags, old army cast-offs and day-glo accessories – all the stuff I later wore on stage.”
Her daughter Celeste Bell says Poly wanted to prove you could be stylish without money — by making your own clothes and buying second-hand.
work: Her lyrics, in her words, were “painting a picture of consumerism with words.” While punk wore black leather, she wore granny cardigans, shift dresses, ankle socks, an army helmet and braces on her teeth.

quotes.text: Some of the things were vile but they were so vile they were cute.
Clothes are never really you, that’s why people wear them… They take you away from reality.
I was just painting a picture of consumerism with words.

why_the_look: Anti-glamour. Plastic, army surplus and thrift as a joke on what shopping promises.
